title: Teaching or a sales funnel?
hookLine: free videos, then a masterclass, then a retreat that costs more than rent: how to tell real teaching from a sales funnel, by the patterns, never the person

lines: FREE, THEN A COURSE, THEN A RETREAT.
IF IT FAILS, YOU DIDN'T COMMIT?
cards: You find someone online who seems to get it. Free videos, a kind voice, real help on a bad week. Then a free masterclass.
Then a course. Then a retreat that costs more than rent, and a creeping feeling that if it isn't working, it's because you didn't commit.
Lately, a lot of people are tired, and some feel burned, after watching well-known spiritual figures fall. That doesn't mean everything you learned was fake. It means it helps to know the signs.
Today: teaching, or a sales funnel?

teach.h: WIDE AND FREE, THEN NARROW AND PRICEY.
teach.b: First, the shape. Marketers call it a funnel: wide and free at the top, narrower and pricier as you go down. There's nothing wrong with a teacher earning a living.
The trouble starts when the teaching exists to move you down the funnel. Second, the warning signs.
They're patterns, not people. A secret only this person can give you. A countdown: the price goes up at midnight.
Guaranteed healing, or guaranteed money. Your doubts treated as the problem: low vibration, resistance, not wanting it enough. Good vibes only, so any sadness counts as failure.
And a quiet pull away from the people who love you. Third, the old tests. Traditions have warned about this for a very long time.

teach.h: BY THEIR FRUITS. SEE FOR YOURSELF.
teach.b: In the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus warns of wolves in sheep's clothing, and gives a test: "Ye shall know them by their fruits."
In a Buddhist discourse, a town called the Kalamas asks the Buddha which visiting teachers to trust. Don't go by tradition or reputation alone, he answers.
See for yourselves what leads to harm, and what leads to well-being. Fourth, what good teaching tends to look like. It says where its ideas came from.
It welcomes questions. It points past itself, like the finger pointing at the moon. It leaves room for grief and doubt.

teach.h: YOU COULD LEAVE AND KEEP WHAT HELPED.
teach.b: And you could walk away tomorrow and keep everything that helped. If someone you trusted lets you down, it's okay to feel betrayed. What was true in the practice is still yours.
The breath never belonged to them.

how: Many traditions test a teacher by the fruits of the teaching: whether it leads to harm or to well-being, whether it welcomes questions, and whether it points beyond the teacher.

o: a teacher's lineage, passed from master to student
a slow narrowing of your focus as you meditate
a sales path: free at first, pricier at each step

games.q: how to test a teaching — tap the pairs.
p: free at the top, pricier going down
a test from the Gospel of Matthew

s: any teacher who earns money is a fraud
earning a living is fine; the trouble is teaching that exists to move you down a funnel.
a price that goes up at midnight is a classic funnel move
urgency is a sales tool, not a spiritual one.
if a practice isn't working, you just didn't want it enough
blaming your doubts is a warning sign, not a teaching.

games.q: a course says your anxiety is low vibration, and the fix is the premium tier, price up at midnight. what's wise?
o: buy now, before the price goes up.
notice the signs, blame, a bigger tier, a countdown, and wait.
hide your anxiety so it stops showing.
games.why: patterns, not people: blaming your doubts, a pricier step, and a countdown are funnel signs. a good teaching will still be there next week.

practice: Bring to mind one voice you turn to for help: a podcast, an account, a book, a teacher.
Ask it three questions, kindly and without judging anyone: does it say where its ideas come from, does it welcome my questions and my bad days, could I leave tomorrow and keep what helped?
Notice the answers, whatever they are, then let it go and just breathe.

wordCard.voice: Funnel, the marketer's word for free at the top and pricier at every step down. Once you know the shape, you'll see it. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: by their fruits. Judge a teaching by what it grows in you, not by the price or the promise. See you tomorrow.
